title: A Time-Bound Preservation-to-Precision Clinical Toolkit: SDF and SMART in Pediatric Dentistry
content: Background. Silver diamine fluoride (SDF) can support caries control, but lesion-level arrest alone does not restore tooth form, sustain function, protect pulpal health, or complete a child’s care. The Preservation-to-Precision (3P) Pathway organizes treatment around these separate responsibilities. [1,2 ] Purpose. This toolkit consolidates clinical, consent, behavioral, home-care, restorative, and administrative documents into a single implementation resource for dental teams caring for children with caries, including children facing barriers to timely treatment. Approach. We consulted selected professional guidance to qualify clinical instructions and update coding terminology. The document is an operational synthesis, not a systematic review or a prospective evaluation. Framework. Care begins with diagnosis, shared decision-making, and a documented purpose for SDF. A 2–4-week response review is followed by risk-adjusted monitoring and explicit 6- and 12-month pathway reviews. These later milestones are proposed accountability checkpoints, not biological expiry dates or universal mandates for restoration. SMART or other treatment can be provided earlier when indicated. Printable templates support consent, aftercare, clinical recording, tracking, and audit. Conclusion. The proposed pathway seeks to prevent temporary stabilization from becoming unexamined deferral. Assess its value through child- and tooth-level outcomes, timely access to indicated care, and transparent reporting of failures and missed follow-up, rather than application counts alone.
